paper_metadata.title: Approximate complex amplitude encoding algorithm and its application to data classification problems

summary: The paper proposes approximate complex amplitude encoding (ACAE) for complex-valued state preparation using a fidelity-based cost function estimated by classical shadows, and applies it to a compact Hadamard classifier. It reports a 5-qubit, 12-layer Iris demonstration with final fidelity 0.994 and a 5-qubit fraud-detection demonstration on a Kaggle credit-card dataset, but provides no hardware benchmark or classical runtime advantage claim.

experiments.description: Approximate complex amplitude encoding (ACAE) used to prepare complex-valued data states for compact Hadamard classifier on the Iris binary classification task (I. setosa vs I. versicolor and I. versicolor vs I. virginica).

algorithm.variant: Approximate complex amplitude encoding (ACAE) + compact Hadamard classifier
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient ansatz with single-qubit Rx/Ry/Rz rotations and CNOT entanglers; test-data encoder uses Ry + CNOT only
algorithm.convergence_criteria: fixed training budget; 400 iterations for training U(θ), 100 iterations for U′(θ′)

hyperparameters.random_initialization: randomly initialize rotation axes (X/Y/Z) and parameters θr
hyperparameters.cost_function: fidelity between model state and target state

algorithm.parameter_initialization: randomly initialize all axes of each rotating gate and θr

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Complex-valued data vector encoded into amplitudes of a 5-qubit state; training data embedded in real and imaginary parts of ancilla-0 branch, test data in ancilla-1 branch
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize fidelity f(θ)=|<Data|ψ(θ)>|^2 for approximate state preparation
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: global phase ignored; compact Hadamard classifier uses ancilla measurement after Hadamard to infer label

problem_instance.description: Binary classification of Iris species using 4 features per sample; two pairwise tasks reported: setosa vs versicolor and versicolor vs virginica

dataset_specification.description: Iris setosa and Iris versicolor: training IDs 1-4 and 51-54; test IDs 5-8 and 55-58. Iris versicolor vs Iris virginica: analogous split with IDs 55-58 and 105-108 shown in results.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: features are used as given; amplitudes normalized to satisfy state normalization
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: single proof-of-principle numerical demonstration; classification results reported for 8 test cases per binary task

implementation_details.classical_solver: Adam optimizer; classical shadow estimation; stabilizer-formalism simulation of Clifford snapshots
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: feature normalization; training/test split selection; random Clifford measurements for fidelity estimation
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: sign of ancilla Z expectation value used as class label

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: fidelity increases to 0.994 by end of training

speedup_claims.factor: avoids O(2^n) state-preparation gates; uses O(poly(n)) gates
speedup_claims.baseline_method: exact amplitude encoding / exact state preparation
speedup_claims.conditions: for approximate state preparation on shallow parametrized quantum circuits
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not prove an end-to-end quantum advantage; classical training of the fidelity estimate still includes an O(2^n) summation.

speedup_claims.factor: fewer gates than original compact Hadamard classifier requiring exponentially many gates for exact initial state preparation
speedup_claims.baseline_method: original compact Hadamard classifier with exact state preparation
speedup_claims.conditions: when using ACAE to approximate the complex-valued data loading
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a circuit-depth/gate-count reduction claim, not a runtime speedup benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: ACAE uses O(poly(n)) gates for approximate state preparation; CHC implementation avoids exponentially many gates for state preparation
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Exact state preparation requires O(2^n) CNOT gates; classical evaluation of fidelity estimate includes O(2^n) summation in training

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware execution or classical-vs-quantum runtime comparison is reported; only a 5-qubit, 12-layer numerical demonstration is given.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline comparison for runtime
State-preparation cost remains exponential in exact form
Classical shadow and Clifford sampling add overhead

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports numerical demonstrations and does not name a real QPU or cloud backend.
num_qubits and circuit depth are reported for the Iris demonstration as n+m+1=5 qubits and a 12-layer ansatz for U(θ).
speedup_order is inferred from the paper's claim of avoiding exponentially many gates for state preparation while not proving an asymptotic end-to-end quantum advantage.
The paper demonstrates a 5-qubit Iris classification example with 12-layer ansatz and reports classification accuracy, but does not show practical quantum advantage over classical methods.
